figures.evidence: The premise 'the two shunt paths replace each other, so one INA228 answers per test' does not follow. IOBoard.md:442 says a test is cabled through one path, but IOBoard.md:503 puts two INA228 on one bus with no switch in a sense path, and a powered INA228 acknowledges its address whatever its IN+/IN-/VBUS are wired to (SLYS021A 7.5.1, Table 7-2). Both answer every test, so 'the monitor whenever it answers' cannot pick the cabled one. The value also says the selector is not stated, yet the tree has one: the ina228_en and one-address ina228_addr settings (shared/settings/settings.c:27-29, :85-95; IOBoard.md:503 'takes one address'). The telemetry-only source on the bring-up module is confirmed (firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:714-725; docs/OpenYGE.md:380-381).

SOVL is 1.25 uV/LSB at ADCRANGE 1 (7.6.1.13): 24,000 counts = 30.00 mV; 150 A x 200 uOhm = 30.00 mV and 300 A x 100 uOhm = 30.00 mV. 30 mV / 202 uOhm = 148.5 A and 30 mV / 105 uOhm = 285.7 A re-derived. F2 (150 A continuous) and V50 (300 A peak, 30 s) read in Research.md. The value states that the trip falls under the rating at upper shunt tolerance.

V288 (owner, 2026-10-01) answers with an operator-set limit on the LIMITS page for each temperature. BVR datasheet Issue 12-September-2024 p2: BVR-Z-R0002 0.2 mOhm, Rthi 4 K/W, TCR 0 +/-20 ppm/K, P 70 degC 12 W, P>100 degC 6 W, so the 4.5 W at 150 A is rated at a 100 degC terminal. 'At least 100 degC' is P2's derived range.

Matches V288's answer word for word: the onboard shunt's sensor, the motor's thermocouple and infrared channels and the ESC telemetry's temperature, each with its own limit. The INA228 die temperature is not in the list.

shared/servo/servo_limit.c:56-62 (hard_limit_a 3.0, stall_above_a 1.0, knee_margin_a 0.15) and shared/servo/servo_sync.c:35-37 (hard_limit_a 4.0) hold positive thresholds only; no negative threshold exists in the tree. Evidence is the absence of a negative use, not a stated owner need.

Thresholds and latching re-derive (see the thresholds and latching entries). The blanking claim does not hold from the datasheet: INA3221 7.3.2.1 says the Critical alert pin 'pulls low if any channel measurement exceeds the limit' on 'individual conversions of each channel' and states nothing on when the pin releases in transparent mode (CEN 0, Table 8-34). The value takes a single over-limit conversion to hold the pin low for at most 3.63 ms and two consecutive ones for 6.6 ms typ, which assumes the pin is held until the same channel converts again. If the pin follows each conversion, a sustained overcurrent on one channel of a three-channel part pulls it low for about one conversion in three (1.1 ms typ, 1.21 ms max), never above the 5 ms blanking, and the port abort never fires. Figure 9-2 shows one channel only. tCONVERT has no minimum, which the value states.

figures.evidence: The figures 3.3 typ and 3.63 ms max a refresh (3 x tCONVERT 1.1 and 1.21 ms, shunt only) re-derive from 6.5 and 7.4.1, and the datasheet gives no minimum conversion time, as stated. figures.evidence: IOBoard.md:624 follows one monitor channel per port; docs/Manifest.md:28 lists INA745A on the servo rail and is superseded. The function takes no part.

Checked against IOBoard.md:74, :453-454, :463-464, :503, the answers V177, V288, V304, and the found values V154, V155, V158 to V161, V165 to V168, V287 whose rows name the Motor monitor. Every requirement is in the list: fixed part, high-side bus and input rating, trip inside full scale, SOVL, latch, 20 ms, alert output, current and voltage accuracy, resolution, charge and energy, reading, addresses, 0 to 50 degC. No value is weaker than its source; the 25 degC calibration in the current accuracy is the found V166's disclosed condition. V179's 85 V fault and V306 sit under External shunt sense input, whose row does not name the Motor monitor. V288's temperatures exclude the INA228 die temperature.
